name: Mazda RX-7 (FD)
h1: Mazda RX-7 FD (third generation): specs, 13B rotary and what owners say

nhtsa.note: NHTSA's complaint and recall model list only has the RX-7 for the 1993 model year, so 1994 and 1995 cars may show no data.

us.x: Sold new in the US for the 1993 to 1995 model years, about 13,900 cars. Later Japanese-market FDs (built to 2002) can be imported once they are 25 years old.

films.x: Dom drives a red 1993 RX-7 to the opening street race. The film used a privately owned car, repainted red so it would stand out.
Orange Julius races an orange RX-7. One of the first film's RX-7s was reused for it with a new body kit and graphics.

gens.tag: 1.3-liter twin-rotor 13B-REW, sequential twin turbos, 255 hp, 8,000 rpm redline.

variants.name: RX-7

trans.note: 4-speed automatic optional on base and Touring; limited-slip standard

variants.what: Limited-slip differential, tape player and cloth seats; cruise control and leather were options.

variants.name: RX-7 Touring
variants.what: Leather, cruise control, sunroof, fog lights, rear wiper and the Bose Wave stereo. The PEP package took its place for 1995.

variants.name: RX-7 R1 / R2
variants.what: R1 for 1993, R2 for 1994-95: stiffer springs, Bilstein shocks, strut bar, extra oil cooling, front lip and rear wing, no sunroof or cruise. Just over 2,600 sold in the US.

13B-REW.name: Mazda 13B-REW
facts: 255 hp at 6,500 rpm, 217 lb-ft at 5,000 rpm (US)
Sequential: one turbo at low rpm, the second joins around 4,500 rpm; boost about 10 psi
Burns oil by design; a metering pump feeds oil into the engine

issues.rx: apex seals?|side seals?|low compression|compression test|engine rebuild
issues.x: A rotary-shop owner told Hagerty that compression shows how worn the engine is. Below 85 psi a rebuild may be close, often from a leaking side seal or a broken apex seal. PistonHeads gives the same advice.
Engine bay heat hardens the many vacuum hoses that run the sequential turbos. Owners interviewed by Hagerty and Driving Line replaced all of them.
issues.fix: Replace the vacuum hoses with heat-resistant ones.

issues.t: Coolant seals and air separator tank
issues.x: PistonHeads says steam from the exhaust at start-up points to coolant seals going brittle with heat. The plastic air separator tank can crack and dump the coolant.
The rotary-shop owner Hagerty spoke to says the engine harness dries out and can cause intermittent electrical faults.
